transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's mostly my hairline, and... the way my face looks under the bright lights at the restaurant where I work. I feel like it makes me look really old and just strange. It's constantly on my mind, even though my coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about when I bring it up.
How convinced are you that the problem with your hairline and face is truly there, despite what your coworkers tell you?

I'm completely convinced. I mean, I know what I see. When I look in the mirror before my shift, it's... it's right there. I know they say they don't notice it, but I just figure they're being polite, or maybe they just don't want to make me feel bad. But there's absolutely no doubt in my mind. It's real.
Do you repeatedly check, groom, camouflage, or compare your appearance because of these concerns?

Yes, I do. Especially before a shift. I'll go into the bathroom and just keep checking the mirror. I take pictures on my phone from all these different angles to see how bad it looks. Then I'll spend I don't know how long trying to comb my hair forward to cover it up. I just keep replaying in my head how the guests are going to see me when I'm standing at the host stand under those lights. I do it so much that half the time I end up being late, or I just get so worked up I can barely bring myself to go out front.
Apart from your concerns about your appearance, do you have any other beliefs that people tell you are not true but that you remain completely certain are true?

No, I don't think so. It's really just... just my hairline and my face. I don't have any other beliefs that people disagree with me on, or anything strange like that. It's strictly just about the way I look.
Is your main belief that you have a specific unacceptable flaw in your appearance, rather than that other people are deliberately reacting to or targeting you because of it?

Yeah, that's right. It's really just about the flaw itself. I don't think people are... out to get me, or trying to target me or anything like that. It's not a conspiracy. 

It's just that I know how bad my hairline and my face look. That's the whole issue for me. I just can't stand that I look this way, especially when I have to be the first face people see at the restaurant. But no, I don't think anyone is deliberately coming after me or plotting against me because of it. It's just the fact that the flaw is there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent preoccupation with perceived appearance defects that others do not observe, accompanied by repetitive mirror checking, photographing, grooming, camouflage, and significant occupational impairment. The complete conviction suggests absent insight/delusional-level beliefs within body dysmorphic disorder; the concern is restricted to appearance and is not part of a broader psychotic or social-anxiety syndrome.

confirmed_symptoms: Constantly thinks about a perceived abnormal hairline and facial appearance.
Believes the perceived defects make the patient look old and strange.
Coworkers do not observe the alleged appearance problems.
Repeatedly checks the appearance in the mirror before work.
Takes photographs from multiple angles to assess the appearance.
Repeatedly combs the hair forward to camouflage the perceived defect.
Mentally replays how guests will perceive the appearance.
Expresses complete certainty that the perceived appearance defects are real despite reassurance from coworkers.
Appearance-related rituals cause lateness for work.
Becomes so distressed that the patient can barely go to the front of the restaurant.
Denies other beliefs that others consider untrue.
Denies beliefs that people are targeting, plotting against, or conspiring because of the appearance concern.

additional_requirements: Preoccupation concerns perceived defects in appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
Repetitive checking, grooming, photographing, camouflage, and mental acts are performed in response to the appearance concern.
The concern is specifically about an appearance flaw rather than a broader persecutory or referential belief.
Delusional-level conviction is present regarding the perceived appearance defect.
